chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The sick person prays sitting. If he is unable, he prays lying down. He says Takbir, then recites. When he intends to bow (Ruku'), he closes his eyes, then glorifies (says SubhanAllah), then opens his eyes, so that opening his eyes is raising his head from Ruku'. When he intends to prostrate (Sujood), he closes his eyes, then glorifies. When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, so that opening his eyes is raising his head from prostration. Then he performs Tashahhud and finishes.
ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform the movements of bowing and prostration while lying down?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual procedure for a sick person performing Salat when unable to stand or bow fully, emphasizing the principle of ease (yusr) in worship. It uniquely prescribes using the closing and opening of the eyes as markers for transitions between Ruku' and Sujood while remaining in a lying position, ensuring the prayer's validity according to Shia jurisprudence. This method highlights the flexibility in physical postures (rukun) while maintaining the essential spiritual intent (niyyah) and recitation.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ibrahim, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The sick would pray Salāt seated. So if he is not able, he should pray Salāt lying down. He should exclaim Takbīr, then recite. So when he intends the Rukū, he would shut his eyes, then Glorify, then open his eyes, so that the opening of his eyes would be his raising his head from the Rukū. So when he intends to perform Sajdah, he would shut his eyes, then Glorify. So when he has Glorified, he would open his eyes, so that the opening of his eyes would be the raising of his head from the prostrations. Then he should perform Tashahhud and finish’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali has narrated from his father from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One suffering from an illness performs Salah (prayer) in a sitting position; if one cannot do this also, one does so while lying on one’s back, says Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) then recites. For Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) closes his eyes, then says Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects), then opens his eyes. Opening one’s eyes is considered standing up from Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees). For Sajdah (prostration) one closes one’s eyes, then says Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects) and then opens one’s eyes which is considered raising one’s head from Sajdah (prostration). Then one says Tashahhud (testimonies of belief) and ends Salah (prayer).”’
